3.0.0.en: The angel of the church: historians mention that the bishop of Sardis was St. Melito.

3.0.1.en: Sardis: a city on a mountain in the region of Asia Minor (Turkey), famous for its shops, its debauchery and its pagan worship associated with licentiousness, like the rest of the pagan lands.

3.0.2.en: The seven Spirits: that is, the One who has the Holy Spirit in fullness; see (ch. 1:4). The seven stars: the seven churches; see (ch. 1:20). The problem of this church or this bishop was the formality and outward show of worship, and for this reason he had a fame and a good reputation, "a name," so the Lord Christ presented Himself here with the theological attribute that suits the state of this church, for He is the One who searches the depths by His Holy Spirit and the One who has authority over all the churches. And the Lord exposes the sickness directly in order to hasten the remedy, and makes clear that the outward appearance does not deceive God even if it deceives men, but if a person remains in this state he is dead, that is, without life before God, and in perdition in eternity if he does not repent.

3.1.0.en: Be watchful: that is, awake and rise from what you are now drowning in, the deception of pride and your spiritual death, and hasten to rescue first the remainder of your life and then the rest of your people who have not died so far. Strengthen: that is, establish them, strengthen them and rescue them from death.

3.1.1.en: That are ready to die: that is, if you do not hasten to repent yourself and your people, the little goodness that remains in you will go away as well.

3.1.2.en: I have not found thy works perfect: that is, the measure is not what men praise you for in outward works but what I, God, examine and judge, and My judgment upon you is your neglect and your turning away from your spiritual striving; and it is also to be noted here that God's judgment and condemnation are on the works of a person, whether hidden or visible.

3.1.3.en: The words here are for all of us... for often we care about what we show before men and forget that God sees what is in secret, so that praise is our portion here, while rebuke and condemnation are God's judgment upon us... May we act upon the remedy that God presents to all of us and watch over our lives and our salvation, for they are the most precious things!!...

3.2.0.en: Remember how: that is, the remedy begins with your remembering your first feelings (ch. 2:4) in your love for God, and how your eagerness and first longings were when you first heard about faith in Me and received the fullness of the grace of the Holy Spirit in Baptism and the laying on of hands (the anointing of the Myron). Hold fast, and repent: that is, after you remember, you must take the next step, which is returning by repentance and putting My commandments into practice and doing them.

3.2.1.en: If therefore thou shalt not watch...: but if you remain in your negligence and your acceptance of praise and your outward worship. I will come on thee as a thief: just as a person does not know when the thief will come to steal from him, so I will come with My punishment quickly at a time you do not expect, [see also what the Lord Christ said about His second coming in (Mt 24:42, 25:5) about the need to watch, not knowing the hour, and the necessity of constant readiness.]

3.3.0.en: Thou hast a few names: although the sin of hypocrisy was widespread in this church, God in His justice does not take anyone for another's fault, and for this reason He declares plainly that there is a small number of true believers whom sin did not touch, since their conduct was pure (white garments), and their reward too will be to accompany Christ in eternity, "they shall walk with me," and Christ will declare their purity before all on the Day of Judgment.

3.4.0.en: He that overcometh, God will reward with the following:

3.4.1.en: 1- He shall be clothed in white raiment: that is, he lives in purity with God forever.

3.4.2.en: 2- I will not blot out his name out of the book of life: that is, he is established in the Kingdom of Heaven, and to explain this phrase further: we believe that when any person comes out of Baptism his name is written in the book of life, that is, the register of the heirs of the Kingdom of God, but the person by his faith, his striving and his works that please God is established in the inheritance of his heavenly Father, whereas he who was negligent and careless and did not watch over the salvation of his soul has his name removed from the inheritance of eternity.

3.4.3.en: 3- I will confess his name before my Father: that is, the Lord Christ will declare in all of heaven "before my Father, and before his angels" the holiness of this person, his piety and his holding to pure conduct in his striving.

3.5.0.en: He that hath an ear: see (ch. 2:7).

3.6.0.en: The angel of the church: he is St. Quadratus.

3.6.1.en: Philadelphia: a city built by the king of Pergamos (Philadelphus) who gave it his name, and it was subject to many earthquakes that impoverished it and made its inhabitants abandon it over the ages.

3.6.2.en: He that is holy, he that is true: the Lord Christ presents Himself here by one of His names and attributes, "the Holy," an attribute that is applied to God alone and no one shares this title with Him, that is, a clear declaration of His divinity, and likewise He is "the True," that is, the One who searches the depths, truthful in His words and just in His judgments. He that hath the key of David: Isaiah prophesied of Christ the Savior and said, "And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open" (Isa 22:22). So the Lord Christ affirms here that He is the one of whom Isaiah spoke by the Holy Spirit, and the expression "the key of David" means the absolute authority of the King, in whose hand is everything, so He opens the Kingdom and the house of His Father to whom He wills and shuts it in the face of the one who does not deserve it.

3.6.3.en: The key of David also comes as an allusion and symbol of the sign of the Cross, which opens to the one who signs himself with it in faith the eyes of the person to the Kingdom, and closes the heart and the senses before Satan and his offers.

3.6.4.en: It can also be said that this key symbolizes the authority given to the Church (Mt 16:19), which is called the authority of binding and loosing, for she alone is the extension of the authority of her Master Christ in opening her doors to repentant sinners and closing them before those who persisted in their error.

3.7.0.en: A little strength: that is, little power, and it is a reference to the small number of people in this church because of the earthquakes or its meager material means, and it can also be said that it is a reference to the weak health of its bishop, so that his bodily strength became little.

3.7.1.en: Since this church had no fame or strong reputation, the Lord Christ began His talk with it with great encouragement; He first presented Himself to it as the possessor of authority (v. 7), and now He gives it the good news that He has opened before it the door of the Kingdom, which no one can shut, and He also praises in the bishop and his church their faith, shown in keeping the commandments of God and doing them and holding to the name of God in the most difficult circumstances.

3.7.2.en: Our beloved God, we thank You from the depths of our hearts for Your love and Your encouragement of us, for we are all possessors of a little strength, very little, and without You we cannot open a door or shut a door, but it is Your promises that fill our hearts with hope.. so come also, my Master, and complete Your work to the full in the life of each one of us and make us hold fast Your name and Your commandments always.

3.8.0.en: Which say they are Jews, and are not: that is, those who claim religiousness and zeal and are not so. See (ch. 2:9). This applies now to all who have departed from the sound faith and claimed that they are Christians, such as the Jehovah's Witnesses and the Adventists and others, who have no aim except to rob the believers from the Church of God... and Christ describes all these here as a synagogue of Satan since they have become his soldiers and the carriers out of his will against the Church. I will make them to come and worship: another encouragement to the Church not to fear these enemies, for Christ alone is able to crush them and humble them and scatter their counsels under the feet of His Church, and they will see and be sure of My love for you and My protection of your church.

3.9.0.en: The word of my patience: an expression meaning that you held to My word in the time of trials and your difficult circumstances.

3.9.1.en: I also will keep thee... the hour of temptation: since you were faithful in the first temptation and held to the faith, you will also be kept and protected from the temptation coming upon the whole world, and what is meant by it is the violent Roman persecution in the time of this church... and this promise can also be generalized to the Church in every time in the face of all persecutions, as long as she is faithful in keeping the commandment of God and shows partiality to no one or accepts a strange faith.

3.10.0.en: Behold, I come quickly: this expression is repeated more than once and means a warning to the negligent of the coming of the just judgment and an encouragement to those who strive and stand firm in their faith.. (see ch. 2:5). Hold that fast which thou hast: stand firm in what you are in and take care lest it be lost, for God's praise and encouragement of us does not mean the guarantee of our salvation, because if we are careless and neglect our salvation we do not escape God's punishment and His just judgment and we lose the Kingdom of Heaven (Heb 2:3).

3.10.1.en: My beloved brother... the previous verse warns all of us against losing the free salvation that Christ offered us, for our accepting salvation does not mean the attainment of eternity; remember Judas who lost his crown, which the Apostle Matthias took in his place, and remember also the birthright which the negligent Esau neglected and the watchful Jacob took, and likewise Demas, the disciple of Paul, who lost everything by his attachment to the present world (2 Tim 4:10).

3.11.0.en: Will I make a pillar: as for the one who overcomes and is victorious, his place will be fixed, "a pillar," and near to Me and to My Father "in the temple of my God."

3.11.1.en: He shall go no more out: that is, whoever reaches eternity has no chance of going out of it again.

3.11.2.en: I will write upon him the name: that is, I declare plainly his belonging to Me, to My Father and to the Kingdom of Heaven, so that his glory is declared before all.

3.11.3.en: The name of my God... the name of the city of my God: this expression may cause confusion for some, for how can Christ have a God, calling Him by the title my God?!

3.11.4.en: What is meant is that the incarnate Christ, as a representative of humanity and as the firstborn among many brethren, calls God "my God," and this is a wonderful humility on His part and a raising of the level of the victorious believers, that Christ should be one of them by His Incarnation and should call God with them his God. And Christ does not mean that He is less than His Father, who gave Him the title God, and the proof is in the following:

3.11.5.en: 1- It is He who said, "I and my Father are one" (Jn 10:30). "He that hath seen me hath seen the Father" (Jn 14:9).

3.11.6.en: 2- The Holy Spirit bore witness to Him: "and the Word was God" (Jn 1:1).

3.11.7.en: 3- In the Book of Revelation itself: "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending" (Rev 1:8). "I am the first and the last" (Rev 1:17). "I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts: and I will give unto every one of you according to your works" (Rev 2:23). "He that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth" (Rev 3:7). And finally, which confirms the equality in the interpretation of the verse we are dealing with, Christ will write His name on "the one who overcomes" just as He will write the name of His Father on him, and this is sufficient proof of the equality of the two names in honor and glory. And let us return once more to the reward in its spiritual understanding... whoever is victorious and overcomes, his reward will be the name of God declared in him, and He is the founder of the heavenly city of Jerusalem, and he also receives the name of the city since he has become an eternal citizen in it, and likewise receives the name of Christ its King.

3.12.0.en: It is the same phrase that the Lord Christ used in all His letters to all the churches.

3.13.0.en: The church of the Laodiceans: the city of Laodicea was the richest of the seven churches and lay between the cities of Colossae and Philadelphia, and was famous for the wool trade, and it took its name from the name of "Laodice," the wife of Antiochus II.. and the material wealth of this church was the cause of its spiritual problem, as we shall see.

3.13.1.en: The angel of the church: in the first age it was succeeded by Aurelius the bishop and then Sapharius the bishop and martyr.

3.13.2.en: These things saith the Amen: "the Amen" here is a title belonging to God alone, and it comes in the meaning of the truth or the One who declares the truth.

3.13.3.en: The faithful and true witness: since the problem of this church was spiritual lukewarmness, and most of the Lord Christ's letter to it is warning and rebuke... the Lord Christ presented Himself here as the witness and examiner of all works, and when He judges, His judgment is final because He is faithful and true; He is not like men, who lack information when they judge, or whose consciences may differ because of partiality or inclinations when judging someone. The beginning of the creation of God: that is, the head, owner and originator of all creation, as St. John said in his Gospel, "All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made" (Jn 1:3).

3.13.4.en: Because this church suffers from spiritual lukewarmness, God declares to it that He is the truth and the true, the head and originator of all creatures, and He is the just One who searches everything and does not accept this slackness.

3.14.0.en: Abundance of money was the basic cause of the slackness of the church of Laodicea, so it sought material pleasure and a life of luxury and left the royal way, which is carrying the cross behind its Master, and fell into spiritual lukewarmness.

3.14.1.en: Thou art neither cold nor hot: a specific divine diagnosis of the sickness of this church, for it is not in spiritual fervor and the spirituality of worship, and it is not cold either in the sense that it does not acknowledge its sin and feel it. I would thou wert cold or hot: for he who confesses and admits his coldness, that is, his sins, may have stirred in him longings of repentance toward God, as happened with Zacchaeus and the Samaritan woman and the sinful woman and the Apostle Matthew, who was a tax collector, and he who is hot there is no fear for him... but you are neither this nor that... and the phrase "I would thou wert cold" reveals to us the seriousness of lukewarmness and spiritual deception, for before God it is worse than a life of sin itself, because the lukewarm person is deceived about himself and content with what he is in, so he does not offer repentance.

3.15.0.en: The Lord used here a material expression to bring the sin of lukewarmness and the state of the lukewarm person closer to our minds.. for just as there are foods that are eaten hot (warm), and kinds that are eaten cold and are palatable, the lukewarm food is what the soul does not accept but spits out.. so the lukewarm person has no taste before God.

3.16.0.en: The Lord Christ makes clear here the cause of the sickness and sin of lukewarmness, for self-regard and wealth entered the heart of this church, and it felt its distinction among the churches and slipped into boasting in its wealth and relied on it, so that it did not feel its real need for God its Savior.

3.16.1.en: And knowest not that thou art: but the truth is that you are not as you see yourself but as I judge you, and I judge you (O lukewarm one) as being:

3.16.2.en: Wretched: from wretchedness, that is, you have no real happiness and inner joy in spite of your wealth.

3.16.3.en: Miserable: because you gave up your divine fellowship and became wretched and in a bad state here and perishing there (eternity). Poor: what is meant is spiritual poverty, in contrast to the church of Smyrna, which was materially poor and whose spiritual riches the Lord praised.

3.16.4.en: Blind: that is, you do not see the truth of your condition.

3.16.5.en: Naked: since you did without My grace and relied on what you have, My grace left you and you became naked, without grace, in want, and you find nothing to cover you before Me.

3.17.0.en: I counsel thee: that is, I offer you a remedy... and it is to be noted that the word "counsel" means that God offers advice to all but does not compel anyone to accept it.. but the person must bear the consequences of his choices... by accepting or rejecting the commandments of God.

3.17.1.en: To buy of me gold: the first of the three remedies that the Lord offered to this church; I alone am the source of giving, so leave the gold of the earth that you rely on, for nothing came of it but your distance and your lukewarmness, for I am the only source of your wealth... and the gold refined in the fire signifies the richness of the spiritual life, and it also signifies Christ Himself, since He alone is the pure gold refined by the fire of the Cross to offer us salvation. White raiment: the second remedy, which is that you must join and be clothed with inner purity, so that you may not be ashamed of your nakedness before Me on the Day of Judgment.

3.17.2.en: Anoint thine eyes with eyesalve: that is, respond to the calls and rebukes of the Holy Spirit, for He is responsible for the spiritual insight of a person, and for this reason one of the titles of the Holy Spirit in our Church is "the Spirit of enlightenment."

3.17.3.en: The summary: the remedy for the sin of lukewarmness can be summarized in the following..

3.17.4.en: 1- Taking refuge in God and declaring my spiritual poverty, so that I acquire God Himself (the refined gold).

3.17.5.en: 2- Striving for purity of heart, without which no one will see Christ.

3.17.6.en: 3- Listening to, responding to and obeying the Holy Spirit of God in our lives, and obeying the commandment and guidance of the Fathers.

3.18.0.en: Since the Lord's words to this bishop and this church were severe words and a hard warning, He returns here and makes clear that the cause of all His words is love, for just as a father disciplines his children, sometimes even with severe rebuke, all he hopes for is their repentance and their return from their error so that they may enjoy life with him and not lose their salvation, and St. Paul also affirms this meaning in his Epistle to the Hebrews, "whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth" (Heb 12:6). Be zealous therefore, and repent: that is, you must care for the salvation of your soul and exert effort in that, and return by repentance to your first way of life.

3.19.0.en: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: a very beautiful picture which makes clear what was explained before, that God respects the will of man and so does not open the door by force, and it also pictures God's longsuffering and patience with us, for He still stands hoping that the person will answer His calls and open to Him (Song 5:2). If any man hear... and open: it is not enough for a person to hear the voice of God and the visitation of His grace to him, but he must rise and open, that is, strive with a sincere will and leave his laziness so that Christ may reign over his house, that is, his heart. I will sup with him, and he with me: he shares with Christ one meal, and this oneness is accomplished by partaking of the Body and Blood of Christ and being satisfied with His holy word.

3.19.1.en: How wonderful is Your love for me, Lord, that supper with me, the sinner, has become the desire of Your heart (Lk 22:

3.19.2.en: 15) "You are the One who stands hoping to enter so that I may open my heart, and You become all mine and I wholly Yours, and the table of Your unlimited love gathers us... is this not what You offer me every day on Your holy altar... O that I would always open my heart with repentance so that You, Bridegroom of my soul, may enter and sup with me and never leave me...

3.20.0.en: To sit with me in my throne: this is the reward of the repentant one who overcomes when he is rid of his lukewarmness, for Christ promises him a reward that exceeds every thought and every imagination! ... for how can we sit with God in His throne, that is, in the glory of His Kingdom!! Is this not a wonderful mystery?... And there is another thing that shows us the power of repentance and its effectiveness... who is it whom Christ will seat with Him... it is the very one He was about to spue out of His mouth; how great are God's mercies and how effective is repentance! He not only forgives sinners but rewards them with what is beyond their expectations or deserving.

3.20.1.en: Even as I also overcame, and am set down: a final word of encouragement in which the Master urges us to overcome and be victorious, for He passed through sufferings and death and came out victorious, and He gave His believing children also the ability to do this by His support of them. And because He overcame in our body, "be of good cheer; I have overcome the world" (Jn 16:33), we also in Him shall overcome and sit with Him in His throne and the throne of His Father.

3.21.0.en: He that hath an ear: the usual conclusion of all the letters, that we may hear and do what we have heard.

3.21.1.en: My beloved brother: the lesson learned from the church of the Laodiceans is not to be preoccupied with material things and boast of them. So we must take care to please the faithful Witness who searches the depths of the heart, instead of spending most of our life trying to please ourselves or to please others at the expense of pleasing our eternity... how serious is the sin of lukewarmness and its punishment... have mercy on us, my God, according to Your great mercy. The throne of God and some of His glory: with the end of the third chapter the first scene of the heavenly vision ends, the scene relating to the pastoral letters to the seven churches; as for the fourth and fifth chapters, they serve as an introduction that carries us to the sixth chapter, where the opening of the seven seals begins, and what the fourth chapter deals with is a description of the throne of God and His glory.
